## November 24, 2026 (latest) — CI: the e2e matrix runs on 16 shards, not 8 (`ci-speed-2utz0n`)

- **Ask (the parent session):** cut PR CI wall time without losing coverage. Push to `ci-speed-2utz0n` only, no PR.
- **Measured before (PR run 45467761411, `264c669`, all green):**
  - The run took 37m55s. The e2e verdict job finished last; WebKit took 16m, jest 9m35s (three full suites back to back), cra-build 2m27s, hostv2-build 1m, backend 37s.
  - The eight shards' test steps took 26.0 to 36.2 min. Setup in each shard is about 1.2 min (checkout, both `npm ci`, `test:unit`, `playwright install`, `e2e:build`). Before the first test, the webServers build the four harness bundles in about 1 min more.
  - Caches: the npm and pip caches hit. Nothing caches `node_modules` or the Playwright browser, and doing so would save seconds per shard, not minutes.
  - PRs run every project on every spec. The merged total was 7494 passed, 540 skipped, 0 failed, 0 flaky.
- **Why the shards were uneven:** the eight blob reports hold 473 min of test work. Playwright's `--shard` splits contiguously by test COUNT, not by time. So shard 7 carried 70 min of work and shard 3 carried 50, and the run waits on the slowest.
- **The change:** `checks.yml` matrix `shard:` goes from 1–8 to 1–16. Nothing else changes: the same specs, projects, `workers: 2`, timeout, job names and verdict job. The denominator is still `strategy.job-total`.
- **The basis:** a simulation of Playwright's split, run on that run's real per-test timings. It put 1800 of 1891 file×project groups in the same shard CI did. Worst shard: 39 min at 8 shards, 25 at 12, 22 at 16.
- **Concurrency:** a run is now 21 jobs. On 11/24, 28 jobs (a PR run and a main run together) started with no queueing.
- **Measured after (Checks run 45479049343, `435fb421`, dispatched on this branch, all green):**
  - The run took **19m43s, down from 37m55s**.
  - The 16 shards' test steps took 13.6 to 17.8 min, and the shard jobs 14.7 to 19.2 min.
  - WebKit took 15m50s, jest 8m45s, cra-build 1m55s, hostv2-build 41s and backend 36s.
  - All 21 jobs started within 1 s of each other, so nothing queued.
  - The merged total was **7494 passed, 540 skipped, 0 failed, 0 flaky**, identical to the baseline.
- **Not built, proposed:** duration-weighted shards would take the worst shard to about 16 min. Playwright 1.61 reads `PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS`, an undocumented test hook, and the weights would need timings refreshed from main. Affected-tests-only on PRs is not proposed: the full suite would still have to run before merge, so it saves nothing on a one-at-a-time merge queue.

## November 23–24, 2026 (test reliability, batch 5) — four e2e root causes: a scrollable card fold, icons the local preview never served, a next-bar reservation that shrank the hero, and a test that aborted its own popup

- **Ask:** two test-reliability problems, root causes, not "flake". Branch `testrel-2utz0n`. Commits `e167bf9`, `6360e23` (11/23); `612d363`, `95ecb1a`, `d45b7ca` (11/24).
- **1. `sendTheDetailsFromYourPhone` (`6360e23`): the app was wrong.**
  - Instrumented (capture-phase pointer log + `.vc-more` scroll state): `pointerdown` hit "Send … the details", `pointerup` hit other card text, and `click` fired on `.vc-more`, so the button never got it.
  - Cause: `.vc-more` was `overflow:hidden`, so the fold was a scroll container. While the card was still opening (`max-height` 0 → 2400px over `--ms-slow`, 550ms), the click's scroll-into-view scrolled the FOLD instead of the sheet (measured `scrollTop` 297; 1228 on the bakery card). As the box grew, the browser clamped the offset back (297 → 37 between press and click) and the button slid out from under the pointer. Keyboard focus and the app's own `scrollIntoView` calls hit the same trap.
  - Fix: `overflow:clip` (with `hidden` kept first as a fallback). It clips the same way but cannot be scrolled.
  - Clipping properly exposed a masked defect: at 390px, a caterer with the send panel open measured `scrollHeight` 3054 under the 2400px cap. "Mark it sent", the link and "Copy link" were cut off for a host; only the e2e reached them, by scrolling the clip box. The cap now lifts at the end of the reveal (`@keyframes vc-uncap`, a discrete step after `--ms-slow`). Closing now snaps shut instead of easing from 2400px.
  - No spec changes, no sleeps.
  - Proof: desktop project, `--repeat-each=60`, 6 workers, 4 busy loops on 4 cores. The two tests failed **5 of 120 before** (4 at "Text Marco", 1 at `[data-send-details-body]`) and **0 of 120 after**; the whole file passed 240 of 240. A first run at `--repeat-each=20` also failed 2 of 80.
- **2. `decisionIdentity` Game Night (`e167bf9`): the icon was never served in CI either.**
  - CI's Chromium is the headless shell, which fetches no page icons. The full Chromium (`PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`) does, and `vite preview` served only `dist`, so `../icon-192.png` (and `../favicon.ico`) returned 404 at `/ngw-event-planner/`. Confirmed both ways: headless shell 18/18 green; full Chromium 3 of 18 red, the first test per worker.
  - Fix: the `ngw-preview-site-root` plugin in `hostv2/vite.config.js`. Under `E2E_BASE` only, it serves `favicon.ico`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png` and `hostv2-manifest.json` from the repo-root `public/`, which is where the deploy serves them from. The console-error assertion is unchanged.
  - Proof: 18/18 on mobile, desktop and tablet-tall with the full Chromium. The `fixtures.mjs` manifest route stays; its comment now points to the plugin.
- **Gates (11/23, superseded):** the "988 passed" full mobile run reported here on 11/23 tested a STALE bundle. The before-measurement swapped the old CSS in, rebuilt, and the fix was restored without a rebuild. The 240/240 after-run predates that swap and stands. Re-run on 11/24 below.
- **3. "Who’s confirmed … each part opens its section" (`612d363`, 11/24): the app was wrong.**
  - Instrumented: `pointerdown` hit the Guests button at y 461; by `pointerup` it was at y 377 with `.app` scrollTop unchanged (1184 = max), and the click went to the section. The hero shrank 1531 → 1447 in the same frame `.app` gained `has-nextbar`.
  - Cause: `.app.app-elegant` is a size container, and `.escreen.on` is `min-height: calc(100cqh - 72px …)`, which reads `.app`’s CONTENT box. `.app.has-nextbar{padding-bottom:84px}` shrank that box, so whenever the hero scrolled away (Playwright’s own scroll-into-view did it) the first screen lost 84px and every row below jumped up 84px. A host scrolling past the hero saw the same jump, against the stylesheet’s own rule ("Anything keyed to .has-nextbar must not alter .app’s BOX").
  - Fix: the 84px reservation moved into the existing `.app::after` scroll-clearance spacer (104 + 84; 160 + 84 with the weather pill). Measured: the hero stays 1531px, the button keeps its content offset, and the last row still scrolls clear of the bar. `spacingLadder` baseline 263 → 262 (`95ecb1a`), its own ratchet for the removed off-ladder value.
  - Proof: under load, whole file, the test failed **8 of 340** across runs on the prior code (uninstrumented: 1/60 and 2/60). After: **400/400** (`--repeat-each=100`).
- **4. `instacartStepsTheList` — "Next" opens the next item’s search (`d45b7ca`, 11/24): the spec was wrong.** It appeared as the one flaky test in the 11/24 full mobile run.
  - Cause: `opened()` aborted every instacart.com request. That left the new tab on Chrome’s network-error page, which reloads itself about a second later and re-requested "Blue crabs" (frame `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`) before the Next tap’s "old bay seasoning" arrived. The app opened one tab per tap.
  - Fix: the helper answers with an empty 200 page. Same request recorded, nothing to retry, assertion unchanged.
  - Proof: mobile, under load, `--repeat-each=100`: **28 of 100 failed before, 0 of 100 after**. Whole file 27/27 on mobile, desktop and tablet-tall.
- **Gates (11/24, on the current bundle):** root jest 920 suites, 13,899 passed, 1 skipped. hostv2 vitest 164/164. Specs touching the hero, next bar, fold, weather pill or `::after` (37 files, mobile + desktop + landscape): 610 passed, 43 skipped. **Full e2e, mobile project: 987 passed, 57 skipped, 0 failed, 1 flaky.** The flaky one is cause 4, fixed after that run in a spec-only change (no rebuild).
- **Running e2e locally in this container:** Playwright 1.61.1 expects headless shell build 1228 and this image has 1243, so set `PW_CHROMIUM`. `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell` is the browser CI uses. `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` is the full Chromium, which also fetches page icons; since `e167bf9` it passes too. Name which one you used when you report.

## November 22, 2026 (late night) — #236: an iPad turned mid-session re-lays out

- **Owner's bug:** iPad Pro 11", Chrome for iOS, live 27b4f740, "Mom's 80th Birthday". After a turn, and then on a fresh landscape reload, the page kept the portrait geometry. Landscape showed an 834pt app with a bare band to its right. Portrait after landscape centered the board in ~1210pt and ran it off the edge. "Request Desktop Site" fixes it.
- **Chrome only.** Safari on the same iPad turns cleanly.
- **Not reproduced in an emulator.** Playwright WebKit at 1194/1210/1366 landscape and 834/1024 portrait, loaded or turned, Wanda or a custom trip, lays out cleanly. Chromium does too.
- **What the screenshots prove (pixel-sampled):** the stage ends at exactly 1668px = 834pt. The ground to its right is #25262A (`--bg-band`), which the body wears only while `(min-width:1024px)` is false. The reload's hero sits at 93pt, which is the 834 tablet centering. So the engine's LAYOUT viewport was 834 in a 1210 window. After the turn, the rail was also up, which needs innerWidth ≥ 1024. Markup and stylesheet disagreed.
- **Fix:**
  - `lib/viewport.js`: the band comes from `matchMedia`, so data-bp/data-rail always agree with the stylesheet. Pinch zoom no longer drops the rail.
  - `hostv2/src/layoutViewport.js`: at load, on a turn, and on bfcache return, it compares the layout width (clientWidth) with the visible width (visualViewport.width; on touch screens also outerWidth, if it fits the screen). If they disagree at scale 1, the viewport meta is pinned to `width=<visible>` and a `resize` is announced. The next turn restores `device-width` first. It writes nothing where the widths agree.
- **Tests:**
  - e2e `anIPadTurnedMidSessionReLaysOut`: 11" and 13", 10 tests, in the WebKit desktop project and in Chromium as self-pinned. It is red on 1659aaee (6 of 8, before the outerWidth case), and the outerWidth case is red-proofed separately.
  - jest `viewport.test.js` covers `readLayoutWidth`.
- 🔴 **Not proven: that iOS lays out at the pinned width.** That is WebKit's handling of the tag. The owner's iPad (mobile mode, landscape reload) is the only check. If it still fails, the page's widths all say 834 and outerWidth does too, and this is a Chrome-for-iOS bug. Try a new tab and Safari.
- **Not changed, on purpose:**
  - `interactive-widget` stays: WebKit ignores the key in Safari and Chrome alike.
  - `100dvh` and an explicit `width:100%` stay as they are. The evidence puts the 834 in the engine's layout viewport (the media queries), not in a box.
- **Welcome full-bleed (Safari iPad, same night):** the first screen drew as a 720pt inset panel at 834 portrait. The cause was the tablet reading measures (`.content` 720/860 and `[data-bp] > .app > .content`) catching `.content.welcome`. It now has `max-width:none`, and the words keep their 30rem column. e2e `theWelcomeIsFullBleedOnATablet` (768, 834, 1032, 1194): red (left 57/86/167) → green, in WebKit and Chromium.
- **Left:** LodgingCockpit's `colCapFor(innerWidth)` still reads innerWidth.

Stripe tests now use real library objects (`construct_from`, `ListObject`) and a real HMAC signature. The library is pinned to `stripe==16.1.0`, the version proven on live.
- 🔴 **Trap: the error middleware hides tracebacks.** A crash in a route becomes a 500 with nothing in the Render log. The message is in `admin_error_log`: `select created_at, message from admin_error_log order by created_at desc limit 5;`.

No auth, billing, profile, Legacy, or production changes. RSVP/Creation/ATTN-2 commits await integration; no release readiness claimed.


**Measured reality, not intentions.** Updated 2026-11-02 (sixtieth entry:
**the People/Attendance redesign arc, and then the owner parked it** — "lets
just get the hostv2 ready for prod and we will pick up the design of the v3
later". 23 commits of People work plus the cover-image record sit on the branch
and change nothing a host sees: `peopleMode` defaults to `false`
(`hostv2/src/HostShellV2.jsx:1116`), so the whole arc is reachable only with
`?people=1`. The finding worth keeping is about the reference material itself:
**the art-direction sheets are generated images, not a design file.** The same
sheet renders the same caption as `MOBILE` in one cell and `ΠABLLE` two cells
over, and the card body copy is not English. Four rounds were spent chasing
pixel parity with an artifact that is not internally consistent. What IS
transferable was measured and applied — the register, per viewport. 🔴 **I
nearly repeated the fifty-ninth entry's exit-code trap in its own next
session**: I ran the gate as `( … > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> log )`, the
subshell's status came from `echo`, and the harness reported **exit 0 on a run
that failed**. Reading the log instead of the status is the only reason it was
caught. See the sixtieth entry.)

Before that, 2026-10-19 (fifty-ninth entry:
**REDESIGN READINESS SPRINT 0 (eight slices) and SPRINT 0.5 (four architecture
decisions)** — and the sprints spent most of their value falsifying their own
predecessors. Sprint 0 planned to BUILD a canonical attendance reader;
`attendanceBand` already was one, returning the exact proposed shape, so none
was built. It planned a needs model as the one true capability gap; three of
four "missing schema" claims were false, all failing the same way — searching
for a module NAMED after a capability instead of for the capability. Sprint 0.5
then found a raw headcount reader that would have written an app-invented count
onto a CONTRACTED caterer and told the host it now matched, and found the permit
advice the app had been giving all along as an INERT note in the frozen shell,
unraised and unanswerable. Verdict: **READY FOR PEOPLE/ATTENDANCE REDESIGN**,
narrower than "ready for the redesign" on purpose. 🔴 **I pushed a broken build
once** — `gate:cra 2>&1 | tail -2 && git commit`: a pipeline's exit status is the
LAST command's, so `tail` succeeding let a commit land on a gate that had
printed "This is a real build error". Every gate since is checked by exit code.
See the fifty-ninth entry.)

Before that, 2026-10-13 (fifty-eighth entry:
PR #90 merged (`5770787`), deploy verified by FETCHING production (bundle moved

first `{"webhook_verified":false}` — confirming the hole had been LIVE for about

Before that, earlier on 2026-10-13 (fifty-seventh entry:

secret set?" had no answer anywhere in the repo. Declared now, with the other
six absences turned into written decisions — including that nobody has recorded
whether production reads PostHog. See the fifty-seventh entry.)

Before that, earlier on 2026-10-13 (fifty-sixth entry —

unverified-dev branch into a free-pass minter on any deployment where

Before that, earlier on 2026-10-13 (fifty-fourth entry:

Before that, earlier on 2026-10-13 (fifty-third entry:
the shell now asks the server whether an event holds a pass, once per event
open, behind two load-bearing guards. The part worth reading is the race it
forced into scope: Stripe redirects the browser and POSTs the webhook
INDEPENDENTLY, so adding a refresh WITHOUT handling that would have revoked the
unlock of a host who paid seconds earlier. A "no" is now provisional while the
event's own blob claims a pass — three asks, not a poll — and the in-flight
dedupe had to become upgradeable or it defeated the fix. Billing is dormant, so
nothing changes in production. See the fifty-third entry.)

Before that, earlier on 2026-10-13 (fifty-second entry:
`passGate` now reads `public.event_passes` through `GET /api/stripe/pass`
instead of only the `ev.passPurchased` boolean on the persisted event blob. The
part worth reading is that **the rule I proposed for it was wrong and I did not
ship it** — "never grant from the persisted event blob" buys no security,
because this gate runs in the browser, and it costs a host who genuinely paid
their unlock on every cold load. What the server record actually buys is
RECOVERY and REVOCATION. Nothing calls the refresh yet, so no runtime behaviour
changed; slice 2 is the hostv2 wiring. See the fifty-second entry.)

Before that, on 2026-10-07 (forty-seventh entry:

all along. Also: the map I said I had hoisted had not been hoisted (a second
copy was added, three keys short, so `lodging` rendered as a capitalized raw
id — and a spec was asserting that fallback as if it were copy); the money row
does not reconcile the way I said; and a tap sweep pointed at the first screen

forty-seventh entry.)

## PARKED 2026-11-02 (sixtieth entry) — four rounds of visual parity against an artifact that is not internally consistent, then the owner pulled the handbrake

Times Eastern (EST, UTC−5 from 2026-11-01 — the row above warned this changeover
was coming and it has now happened).

### What the 24 commits are, and why they are safe to carry

23 of them are the People/Attendance redesign and its calibration documents;
`eb4f9e0` is the cover-image record. **None of it is reachable in production.**
`peopleMode` is initialised `false` at `hostv2/src/HostShellV2.jsx:1116` and only
`?people=1` flips it, the same opt-in shape the repo used for `?demo=lodging`
and `?elegant=0`. So the branch can merge whenever the owner wants without
changing one pixel a host sees. **That is worth stating plainly because the
branch is now 45 commits ahead of `main` and nothing has shipped since
2026-10-13** — the cost of not merging is not design risk, it is that Sprint 0,
Sprint 0.5 and the People work are all sitting where no deploy can reach them.

### 🔴 THE REFERENCE SHEETS ARE GENERATED IMAGES, AND FOUR ROUNDS WERE SPENT BEFORE I CHECKED

The owner supplied art-direction sheets and said three times, in three separate
rounds, "we still don't have parity". Each round I measured a different part of
them, matched it, and was told the same thing again. The loop did not terminate,
and the reason is not that the work was sloppy:

| Evidence | Where |
|---|---|
| The caption under one device reads `MOBILE`; the same caption two cells over reads `ΠABLLE` | `ref-place-journey.png`, row 1, cells 2 and 3 |
| Card body copy is not English — *"Yoar evect needs enough cnoture to kaag plaming managable wiBoxd ndentation feel generc."* | same sheet, cell 1 callout |
| The tablet's display type (≈87px) is LARGER than the desktop's (≈78px) | `ref-team-responsive.png`, measured |

**They are concept renders, not a design file.** There is no underlying type, no
consistent metrics, and no responsive system — the three devices were drawn
independently, which is why the tablet inverts. Pixel parity with them is not a
reachable target, and four rounds of chasing it is the cost of not checking the
artifact before trying to match it. **The next session must not restart that
loop.** What they legitimately carry is direction: a register, a palette, a
photographic treatment, a device-cascade presentation.

### What the gap actually was, measured

Not chrome. I spent three rounds on nav bars, hamburgers, status bars, row
anatomy — all real, all matched, none of it the problem. The problem was
**register, and it was per-viewport**: every device was sharing one 34px display
and one 14px body, so the tablet was a desktop shrunk 73% rather than a tablet.

| | Supplied sheets | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display cap as a share of frame width | 3.8% / 5.9% / 7.0% | — | — |
| Display type (1440 / 1024 / 390) | ≈78 / ≈87 / ≈39px | 34 / 34 / 23 | **78 / 64 / 39** |
| Body + spacing scale | — | 1.0 across all three | **1.50 / 1.35 / 1.12** |
| Photographic band | 26.6% / 24.0% / 26.7% | 18.9% everywhere | **26.6 / 24.0 / 26.7** |

⚠️ **The 18.9% photo band this file's redesign docs carry came from the JOURNEY
sheet; the two RESPONSIVE sheets say 26.6%.** The owner's own sheets disagree
with each other — further proof of the independent-render finding. The
responsive pair wins for anything cross-device, because they are the only ones
showing three devices of one screen.

### The ruling that was made and then parked before it was written down

Asking for parity with the sheets is, in effect, ruling against `UX_01`'s
*"Desktop is denser, not wider"* and its display-tier-only serif rule, and
against `UX_02`'s steel accent. The owner said **"correct both in the repo"** —
and then, before any edit was made, **"stop … lets just get the hostv2 ready for
prod"**. So:

🔴 **`UX_01` and `UX_02` still contradict the ruled direction, in writing, in
files that are mandatory reading for every UI task.** Nothing was edited — the
working tree was clean when the stop came and no correction was half-applied.
The three specific lines are: `UX_01` "No white backgrounds anywhere … Studio
Matte is dark-on-dark" (false since light mode shipped 2026-09-28, independent
of any ruling), `UX_01` "Desktop is denser, not wider", and `UX_02`'s
`Steel blue | C.accent` row. This is the exact failure the workspace
`CLAUDE.md` scar records — a mandatory-reading file left false — and it is open
on purpose rather than by oversight.

### 🔴 THE EXIT-CODE TRAP, REPEATED IN THE VERY NEXT SESSION

The fifty-ninth entry records: *"a pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's,
so `tail` succeeding let a commit land on a gate that had printed 'This is a
real build error'. Every gate since is checked by exit code."*

I ran this session's gate as:

```
( npm run verify:fast > verify_fast.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> verify_fast.log )
```

The subshell's exit status is `echo`'s. **The harness reported the background
task as "completed (exit code 0)" on a run whose own last line reads
`✗ 1 of 10 failed` / `EXIT=1`.** Same class of defect, one entry later, in a
different shell construct — the lesson had been recorded as being about
pipelines, and it is actually about *anything that puts a command after the one
you care about*. It was caught only because the log was read rather than the
status. **Put the gate LAST in any wrapper, or capture its status before
anything else runs.**

| Matrix | **GREEN — 3,136 passed / 273 skipped / 0 failed / 1 flaky, 54.5m**, seven projects, run after this entry was first written. The flaky re-ran 20/20 clean in isolation. `PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` was all the pin gap ever needed |

### 🔴 PRODUCTION PROBE 2026-11-02 — the backend is on a tier that sleeps, and guests are the worst traffic for it

Nobody had probed production today, so it was probed rather than assumed.

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Pages `https://twillis45.github.io/ngw-event-planner/` | **200**, serving `static/js/main.69037cdc.js` |
| That bundle | **the same one the fifty-eighth entry recorded on 2026-10-13** — measured confirmation that nothing has shipped in 20 days, not an inference from the branch state |
| Backend `/health`, first two calls | **timed out at 45s, no bytes received** |
| Backend `/health`, third call | **200 `{"ok":true,"service":"ngw-events-api"}` in 14.3s** |
| Backend `/health`, warm | **0.28s, 0.59s** |
| `render.yaml:9` | `plan: free` |

**The service spins down.** Cold-to-warm is a ~75x latency difference, and the
first caller after an idle period eats a 30-60s wait with nothing on screen.
I did not conclude "the backend is down" from the first two timeouts — the
cold-start hypothesis was separated from an outage by simply waiting longer,
which is the only reason this reads as a tier finding instead of an incident.

**Why this matters more than a normal latency note: the sporadic caller is the
GUEST.** `GET /api/public/invite/{code}` is served by this same instance, and
guests arrive one at a time, days apart — the exact traffic shape that
guarantees a cold instance. A host demoing the product hits a warm service
because they just used it; the guest opening the invite does not.

**The defect I went looking for does NOT exist, and that is worth recording.**
The hypothesis was that a cold 5xx would render the existing "link not found"
fallback — telling a guest their invite is dead because the server was asleep.
`src/lib/api/rsvp.js:61` already carries `INVITE_FETCH_FAILED`, a sentinel that
separates "the server says no such invite" (404 / ok-but-empty → null) from
"the lookup failed" (5xx / network → retryable), with the reason written at the
line: *"a transient blip is retryable and must not be shown as 'this link is
dead.'"* So the guest waits; they are not lied to. Checked, not assumed.

What remains is latency, and it is an owner-side spend decision rather than a
code change. It is **not currently on any stage-9 list**, and it should be:
precondition #4 is a live-keys purchase, and a checkout call into a sleeping
instance is the first impression a paying host gets.

Also verified while in there, both already correct: no client-side fetch
timeout on the invite call (so the guest waits rather than erroring), and the
public RSVP entropy floor is real — `MIN_CODE_LEN = 16` enforced before the
query runs (`backend/app/routers/rsvp.py:230`), with new events minting 22-char
tokens. Rate limiting on that route would be defence in depth, not a blocker,
so none was invented for it.

### Two defects the probe turned up, both fixed, both invisible to every existing check

**1 · The parse gate's ceiling was under its own cost.** `shellParses.test.mjs`
ran `../src/HostShellV2.jsx imports cleanly` on vitest's 5000ms default and
failed about one run in two — always a TIMEOUT, never an assertion. Measured
with the ceiling lifted: **6101 / 6088 / 5691 ms**. Systematically over budget,
passing only when the machine squeezed under. It first went red while an
unrelated change was in flight, so the tree was STASHED and the clean tree
reproduced 2-of-3 red on its own — the change was exonerated by measurement
rather than by argument. Raised to 20s (~3.3x worst case, still a hang
detector), **5/5 green after**. A gate that fails half the time is worse than
no gate: it teaches whoever hits it to re-run until green, which is the habit
that lets a real failure through.

**2 · hostv2 had no tab icon, and the 404 was invisible by construction.** The
live shell was driven in a real browser at 390px — it boots, renders, 0 failed
requests — with one console error reproduced 3/3: `Failed to load resource:
404`, no URL. No URL because **no response listener ever saw it**. The head
declared `rel="manifest"` and `rel="apple-touch-icon"` but no `rel="icon"`, so
Chromium fell back to the ORIGIN root, `twillis45.github.io/favicon.ico` — the
GitHub user-site root, not this project's. A browser-initiated favicon fetch
raises no page response event, so every check that watches network traffic was
structurally blind to it and the only trace was a bare console line. Fixed with
`rel="icon"` on both favicon.ico and icon-192.png, **both verified 200 live
before being referenced**.

Also verified in the same probe and already correct: all **11 service-worker
precache entries resolve 200** (the offline shell is intact), and hostv2 is
live and serving at `/hostv2/`.

### GOLD-09 and two thirds of GOLD-10 closed — the money path finally has a browser

The owner's read was right: scenario coverage was incomplete. Measured against
`docs/architecture/current-state/GOLD_E2E_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md`, which scores
ten end-to-end scenarios, and the worst open row was the one under the money.

🔴 **GOLD-09: the pass entitlement had ZERO browser coverage.** A grep across
all 133 specs for `passGate|event_passes|passPurchased|stripe` returned one
hit, a negative control in the demo spec asserting a demo id is NOT a
purchase. Stage-9 precondition #4 is a live-keys Stripe purchase: the money
path was about to be switched on with no browser having walked it.

**Why it survived two green unit suites, and this is the part worth keeping.**
`passGate.js` answers "allowed" at every gate while `isBillingLive()` is false,
and that needs BOTH a truthy API base and `REACT_APP_BILLING_LIVE === '1'`.
The shared e2e bundle carries neither. Driven against it, the pass sheet reads
**"fully unlocked right now"** — a spec written there passes having executed
none of the entitlement path. The unit suites drive the MODULES; nothing drove
the SHELL. So: its own bundle (`.env.passgate`, port 5266) and a premise test
that goes red if that bundle ever loses the switch.

Seven tests. The race is the reason it exists — Stripe redirects the browser
and POSTs the webhook independently, so a host who just paid can land with the
blob claiming a pass and the row not written. **Red-proofed rather than
observed:** claim present with answers F,F,T gives 3 asks and ends unlocked;
claim removed with the same answers gives 1 ask and ends locked. Remove the
thing under test and it fails.

**GOLD-10: two of three closed, and the third is NOT claimed.** Write failure
and invalid route now have guards; producer failure does not and is written
down as still open. The write is the one that matters: HostShellV2's own
comment says quota-exceeded is realistic rather than theoretical because a
patch carries photos, and "swallowed, the host keeps editing an event that is
no longer being saved and finds out when they reopen it." Measured on a real
boot with `setItem` throwing for `ngw-hostv2-patch-*` only: **2 failed
attempts, exactly 1 notice**, naming cause and remedy. The dedupe is asserted
separately because it is the regression-prone half.

⚠️ **An instrument that lies is worse than no instrument.** The save-failure
toast auto-dismisses AND arrives inside a re-rendered subtree. Sampling at the
end found nothing; a MutationObserver on `addedNodes` also found nothing. Both
were tried here and both reported a clean run against a shell that was warning
correctly — i.e. both would have recorded the opposite of the truth. An 80ms
poll across the run is what sees it.

**Two bugs of mine on the way, both recorded at their lines.** The catch-all
Playwright route was registered AFTER the specific stub, so it swallowed every
`/api/stripe/pass` call and the suite reported zero asks — reading exactly like
"the shell never asked". That is the fifty-ninth entry's own trap, quoted
earlier in this same session and still written backwards. And the first
control arm only counted writes when it was also throwing them, so it asserted

### GOLD-06 closed, and it closed GOLD-10's last third with it

Weather IS a producer, so "the weather surface tells the truth" and "a
producer failure is handled honestly" turned out to be one contract read from
two sides. GOLD-06 is the row the Sprint 0 verdict cites as the reason BOTH
its verdicts were scoped, and it had no browser guard.

The rule under test is the module's own: *"a configured app shows live weather
or nothing — a fabricated fallback could contradict the real sky"*, and the
catch that swallows a provider failure says *"stay quiet — no forecast beats a
wrong one."* The failure that prevents is concrete: an app wired to a real
forecast, provider down, quietly showing a SAMPLE the host reads as the real
sky, who then plans a 30-person outdoor party against invented rain.

**No new bundle.** `isWeatherConfigured()` is
`Boolean(REACT_APP_OPENWEATHER_KEY || REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL)`, so 5233 is the
unconfigured arm and GOLD-09's passgate bundle on 5266 is the configured one.
Same event, same fixture, same boot; configuration is the only variable.

| Arm | Provider called | Sample label |
|---|---|---|
| Unconfigured | **never** | **shown, and labeled** |
| Configured + 500 | **yes** (`geocode`) | **absent** |

⚠️ **The provider-call assertion is the load-bearing one, and the first run
proved why.** The venue NAME is `ev.venue`, not `ev.venueName`
(`venueFor.js:39`). With the wrong key `isLikelyOutdoor` is false, the whole
effect returns early, and the spec read CLEAN ON BOTH ARMS — a false pass on
both sides of a differential at once, which is the worst outcome a test like
this can have. Counting the calls makes that impossible: no calls means the
path never ran, and the silence proves nothing.

### A save never silently overwrites — census §5's three-month-old NOT MET, closed on the disclosure half

LIVE_MODE_CENSUS §5 (2026-08-08) scored "concurrent edits resolve without
silently discarding one" as NOT MET: every cloud write was a blind
`upsert(..., { onConflict: 'id' })`, last-write-wins on the whole blob, and
"nothing surfaces that." It sat on no stage-9 list. The cloud→local half was
already honest (hydrate adopts a newer copy and says so, never over a dirty
local one); this is the local→cloud half.

**Mechanism** (`src/lib/api/events.js`): `loadEvents` carries the row's
`updated_at` as `_cloudUpdatedAt` (provenance, same convention as `_sample`;
stripped from `data` on every write so the blob never carries a stale copy of
its own column). `saveEvent` with a known version is a conditional UPDATE —
`.lte('updated_at', version)` — and zero rows matched answers
`{ ok:false, queued:false, reason:'conflict', loadedAt, serverUpdatedAt }`.
Not thrown, not queued (retrying a refused overwrite refuses again), the
edit already in the local store. `syncState` gained `SYNC_STATUS.CONFLICT`
("Changed somewhere else — your edit is on this device only"), which outranks
an older success stamp and is cleared by the next real success. A queued
write meeting a newer row leaves the queue by name (`error:'conflict'`).

**🔴 THE FIRST CUT MADE A DEVICE REFUSE ITSELF, and it was measured, not
guessed.** hostv2's `patchEvent` saves on every keystroke with no debounce, so
the second write started before the first write's new stamp was back, carried
the loaded stamp, met a row its OWN first write had moved, and came back
`conflict` — the host would have been told "changed somewhere else" by their
own typing. Two fixes, both in the lib so both shells get them: writes to one
id are CHAINED (second starts after the first settles), and the newest version
this device produced or saw is kept per id in `ngw-cache-stamps` and used when
newer than the event's own stamp — which is what makes the frozen CRA shell
(ignores every save result; adopts no stamp) safe too, and survives a reload.
Red-proofed one guard at a time: chain removed → the two-in-flight test red;
`.lte` made always-true → the three refusal tests red; stamp record removed →
the CRA-pattern test red. (The first `.lte` red-proof DELETED the clause and
got a red that was the mock talking — it refuses any write without an `.lte`
— so it was re-run as always-true, which is the proof that counts.)

**CRA, deliberately touched.** `src/App.js` is frozen, but "security/data-loss
fixes" are the carve-out and this is one: its debounced saver `Promise.all`ed
`saveEvent` and reported "saved" on resolve — which, with a refusal that
resolves instead of throwing, would have shown ● Saved over an edit the cloud
had refused. It now reads the results: any `reason:'conflict'` → `sync_failed`
+ a one-line toast naming where the edit is. One `.then` body; nothing else in
the file moved.

**Where it reaches runtime UI.** hostv2: `noteSaveResult` adopts the returned
stamp into the custom copy and toasts the refusal once per session; hydrate
compares CONTENT (stamp stripped) so a device's own save is never announced as
"updated from your account", and adopts a newer stamp silently when content
matches. CRA: the banner + toast above.

**What it is not.** Not a merge — the losing edit is kept and named, never
folded in. Not browser-driven: no e2e drives two real sessions against one
row; the 11 jest tests use a mock of the exact chains, and the version
comparison they exercise is the real one. `migrateLocalToCloud` stays blind
(a migration has nothing to compare). Census §5 and `LIVE_MODE_READINESS.md:56`
both carry the re-measurement; the checkbox stays unchecked until a browser
proves it.

### 🔴 Six public tables with RLS OFF — found by writing the owner's attestation query, fixed in repo, NOT yet on the live project

Writing the three owner attestations into `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (§ Owner
attestations: RLS applied, backups + restore drill, login rate limits, plus the
two telemetry arrivals — each as a query or page, with what a pass and a fail
look like and where to write the result) meant writing the RLS query first and
predicting its output from the migrations. The prediction had six `false`
rows: `supabase/migrations/012_research_execution.sql` creates
`research_campaign_runs`, `research_queue_jobs`, `research_findings`,
`research_evidence`, `research_observations` and `provider_run_logs` with no
`enable row level security`, on the comment "all reads/writes go through
FastAPI with require_admin — no RLS needed." That reasoning sees one door.
PostgREST is the other: every `public` table is served at `/rest/v1/<table>`,
and Supabase's default privileges grant `anon`/`authenticated` on it, so with
RLS off the publishable anon key — in the live bundle by design — can read
and WRITE those six. Enqueue research jobs (provider spend), rewrite findings,
read every campaign blueprint.

**Why nobody saw it:** the checklist's "DONE — RLS verified in writing" row
named the tables it checked and never claimed "every table." Nobody asked the
complement until a query that lists every table was being written. The
attestation runbook earned its keep before the owner ran it.

**Fix:** `018_research_tables_rls.sql` — RLS on, no policies, the exact shape
`admin_error_log` and `kas_records` already run on with the backend inserting
through its owning role (non-forced RLS does not apply to the owner), so the
research router is untouched. Nothing client-side reads these tables (zero
hits in `src/`, `hostv2/src/`). **Gate:**
`src/lib/__tests__/everyPublicTableHasRls.test.js` reads both migration
folders and fails by table name on any `create table` without a matching
enable; red-proofed by removing 018 (7 of 10 red, all six named). The backend
folder passes too — every legacy table already had RLS.

**What is NOT done, and only a merge does it:** the Supabase GitHub
integration applies `supabase/migrations` from `main`. Until 018 is merged the
live project is presumed exposed. **Could not be probed from here:** the public
Pages bundle is the demo profile and carries no Supabase URL or anon key
(checked by fetching `main.cbde5e5e.js`, 5.67 MB, and grepping it), and the
owner's project URL is not in this repo. Check A's query in the runbook is how
the owner confirms it closed. Recorded in
`docs/audits/2026-08-21_SECURITY_TRACK_CHECKLIST.md` as a new stage-5 row.

### The conflict path, driven in a browser — and the lie the red-proof exposed

`hostv2/e2e/aRefusedSaveIsNotCalledSaved.spec.mjs` (2 tests, desktop-only,
on crossDeviceSync's 5244 fake-cloud harness). A real tap — the Guest list
sheet's "By list" toggle, one `patchEvent` — goes out as a conditional UPDATE
with `updated_at=lte.<version>` on the wire (asserted off the request URL, not
inferred), the stub answers zero rows and a newer `updated_at`, and the shell
must: toast the refusal in words that name where the edit is, keep the edit
locally, queue nothing, and show "Changed somewhere else — your edit is on
this device only" in the settings row. The control runs the same tap with the
row unmoved: silent, "Synced", and the new version adopted into the local
copy. **Red-proofed by removing the shell's conflict branch and rebuilding the
bundle:** test 1 went red with the toasts it saw —
*"Saved on this device — it will reach your account when the connection is
back."* That is the sentence the shell says for a refused write when the
branch is absent, and it is false in both halves: the edit will not reach the
account, and the connection was never the problem. The jest tests could not
have seen it; only the shell says it.

`activationFunnel.spec.mjs` gained the **`event_created` gate** the stage-7
card has carried as open since 2026-08-29 ("no create door reachable from a
seeded boot"). The door exists now; a clean device, Start my event, a typed
seed, Put my plan together → exactly one `event_created`, `is_first: true`, a
string `event_type`, and the town / setting / count typed never in the payload.
The first cut asserted the words "crab feast" did not leak and went red on
`event_type: "Crab Feast"` — the playbook TYPE is a label, not the host's
words; the assertion now names what would actually be a leak.

🔴 **Three harness traps, each paid for once this session.** (1) Tapping the
Guests tile opens a SHEET over the plan card, so locators that match the
card's chips resolve and then time out behind the dialog — scope to
`.sheet[role=dialog]`. (2) A scratch Playwright config outside `hostv2/`
cannot resolve `@playwright/test` (import it by absolute path) and needs the
real `baseURL` including `/ngw-event-planner/hostv2/` — the wrong base made
eight pre-existing funnel tests time out at once, which is how you tell a
harness fault from a product one. (3) `pkill -f "vite preview --outDir
dist-synctest"` inside a `bash -c` string **matches and kills its own shell**
(exit 144) — and that run had already removed the conflict branch from
`HostShellV2.jsx` for the red-proof, so the source sat modified until
restored from the backup. Bracket one character (`dist-synctes[t]`) so the
pattern cannot match itself; the red-proof was re-run as a script file and the
restore diffed identical.


definition and local cannot drift from CI.

### Traps worth the next session's time

- **A pipeline's exit status is the last command's.** `cmd | tail -2 && commit`
  commits on a failed `cmd`. This is how I pushed a broken build (`b8ea88c`
  fixes it). Check gates by exit code.
- **`vendorAccountability/` needs fully-specified ESM imports** (`.js`
  mandatory). jest resolves extensionless; webpack there does not — so the unit
  suite is green while the CRA build fails.
- **`export { x as y } from '…'` creates NO local binding.** `eventPool.js`
  carries the measured record of what that cost; I nearly repeated it in
  `seatingPlan.js`.
- **`addInitScript` re-runs on every navigation**, so an unconditional seed
  erases what the test just did on `page.reload()`.
- **Playwright tries routes most-recently-registered FIRST** — a catch-all must
  be registered before the specific mocks it should lose to.
- **jest rejects a second argument to `expect()`** (that is Vitest/Playwright).
  I hit this twice, in two different sprints.
- **`innerText` reflects CSS `text-transform`** — `.shelf-label` is uppercased,
  so assert case-insensitively.

## THE UNATTESTED QUESTION GOT AN ANSWER, THEN THE ANSWER CHANGED — BOTH MEASURED

The probe this session built answered, minutes after the deploy, the question
the 2026-10-03 audit could not and no file could, because the variable was not
declared anywhere (the entry below):

```
$ curl .../api/stripe/status      # ~13:25 Eastern, just after the merge
{"configured":true,"webhook_verified":false,"can_honour_purchases":false}

$ curl .../api/stripe/status      # after the owner set it on Render
{"configured":true,"webhook_verified":true,"can_honour_purchases":true}
```

**`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` IS NOW SET.** Both readings are kept because the first
one is the evidence and the second is the state. **This is the single most
useful thing the session produced** — not the code, the answer: a question that
had been unanswerable all day became one curl.

⚠️ **A PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE RESULT.** This entry was drafted with
the heading "THE ANSWER IS NO: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET IS NOT SET IN PRODUCTION",
and it was corrected before commit because the value flipped while it was being
written — the Render redeploy had simply not restarted the process yet when the
first probe ran. A `false` from this probe can mean "not set" OR "set, not yet
redeployed", and nothing in the reading distinguishes them. **Re-probe after a
redeploy before concluding anything from a false.** Had this shipped unchecked
it would have been a wrong headline in the file whose whole job is measured
truth — the exact failure the stale header and stale gate table below record.

**THE FIRST READING CONFIRMS THE HOLE WAS LIVE, and that is why it is kept.**
`configured: true` with `webhook_verified: false` is precisely the state the
security fix was written for: secret key set, signing secret absent, and
`_grant_pass` deployed since 07:41. For roughly six hours this morning, a charge
on that deployment would have taken $39 and recorded nothing, and an unsigned
POST to the webhook would have minted a pass for any event in any studio. The
dashboard agreed independently — Stripe Workbench showed **no webhook endpoint
at all** and "no deliveries in the last 7 days". Two sources, same conclusion.

**WHAT `can_honour_purchases: true` DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN.** It means a secret
EXISTS. It does **not** mean the secret matches the key creating the sessions —
see the sandbox trap below. The probe cannot see that, and only a real test-mode
checkout end to end can. Do not read the green as "sellable".

**A SECOND TRAP FOUND IN THE DASHBOARD, worth more than the first.** The owner's
Stripe context is a **SANDBOX on test keys** (`sk_test_…KoTp`), and Render's
`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is **a different key** — context unknown, prefix unreported
at the time of writing. Stripe sandboxes are ISOLATED: an endpoint created in
one fires only for sessions created with that one's key. So pasting a `whsec_`
from the sandbox while Render holds a foreign key produces the worst failure
shape available: `can_honour_purchases` flips **true**, the buy button appears,
and every real webhook is rejected 400 — the original "charge with nothing
recoverable" wearing a green badge. **The probe can see that a secret exists,
never that it is the RIGHT one.** Ruling: align Render to the chosen sandbox
rather than reverse-engineer the mystery key; an unidentified key in production
is a liability on its own, and replacing a test key on a dormant product costs
nothing.

**STILL OPEN, and none of it is code:**
· **confirm the destination's payload style is SNAPSHOT, not thin** — the
  handler reads `event.data.object.metadata` directly, so a thin payload
  delivers no `studio_id` and silently grants nothing while returning 200;
· confirm it subscribes `checkout.session.completed`, the only event
  `_grant_pass` runs on;
· confirm the `whsec_` came from the SAME context as the secret key — the probe
  reads green either way;
· whether migration `017` ever applied to live Supabase — still unattested, and
  if the table is absent the insert raises and the grant is inert;
· a real test-mode checkout end to end, which is the ONLY thing that proves the
  secret matches the key. D-2 #5 regardless.

**THE RUNBOOK FOR THAT LAST ONE EXISTS NOW:**
`docs/ONE_EVENT_PASS_PURCHASE_RUNBOOK.md`, written at the owner's request.
Eight steps, every factual claim checked against source rather than recalled
(the hostv2 dev port 5199, `.gitignore` line 17, `CLAIM_RETRY_DELAYS_MS`,
`PASS_AMOUNT_CENTS`), plus a failure-mode table keyed on the **delivery-log
status code** — 400 means the `whsec_` is from the wrong Stripe context, 500
means migration 017 never applied, 200-with-no-unlock means a thin payload, and
no delivery at all means the event is not subscribed. One purchase settles all
four of the unproven items above, and each failure mode points at exactly one of
them. It also insists the result be recorded here WITH that status code, because
"it worked" without the number is the claim this file keeps having to
re-measure.

**NOT DONE, AND OFFERED:** adding `mode` (`"test"`/`"live"`, from the key
prefix — not secret material) to the status probe, which would make the
test-vs-live half of that mismatch visible from one curl. Proposed and awaiting
the owner's word; it cannot identify WHICH sandbox, only the mode.

## FIXED 2026-10-13 (fifty-seventh entry) — the money keys were the only secrets the blueprint never named

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). The missing half of the entry below.

**`render.yaml` IS THE RENDER BLUEPRINT — deploying from it PROMPTS for every
`sync: false` variable.** Its own header says so. It named **8 of the 16**
environment variables `backend/app/config.py` reads, and among the missing were
**`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`**. The money keys were the
only secrets the file did not name.

So a fresh Blueprint deploy was never asked for either one, and Stripe would
come up silently unconfigured — while the 2026-10-03 audit recorded production
as `{"configured":true}`, which means a dashboard value no file in this repo
records. **That is why "is the webhook secret set?" was unanswerable**: the
variable did not exist anywhere a reader could find it. The fix in the entry
below made the question *checkable* over HTTP; this makes it *declared*.

Three keys added, each with what UNSET means, in the file's existing voice:
`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (with the note that it is the
difference between a paid pass being recorded and the grant being refused), and
`RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — which config.py already documented as "If unset,
verification is skipped (dev/testing only — set this in production)", the same
shape as the Stripe one, missing for the same reason.

**THE OTHER SIX ABSENCES ARE NOW DECISIONS RATHER THAN SILENCES.**
`theBlueprintNamesWhatTheServerNeeds.test.js` requires every variable the server
reads to be declared **or** carry a written reason — the `CALLED_FROM_OUTSIDE`
idiom. Real reasons, not filler:
· `ALLOW_DEV_TOKEN` — **deliberate security omission**, and render.yaml already
  said so in capitals: declaring it would put the `X-Planner-Token` bypass one
  dashboard field away from being switched on in production.
· `SUPABASE_DB_URL` — an alternative spelling, not a second variable
  (`DATABASE_URL or SUPABASE_DB_URL`); naming both prompts twice for one string.
· `RESEND_FROM_NAME` — non-secret display string with a working default.
· `POSTHOG_QUERY_API_KEY` / `POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID` / `POSTHOG_QUERY_HOST` —
  **an open decision, stated as one**: nobody has recorded whether production
  reads PostHog. If the admin funnel is meant to work there, these three belong
  in the blueprint. Written down so it is a question somebody can answer rather
  than three variables nobody notices.

Two tests beyond the sweep earn their place: a **commented-out** example is not
a declaration (render.yaml carries one for `ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEX`, and a matcher
that counted it would congratulate itself on a comment), and **no `value:` line
may contain a live secret prefix** — `sk_live_`, `whsec_`, `phx_`, a postgres
URL — which checks the header's "never commit secrets" promise instead of
trusting it. The money keys are also asserted **by name**, because a general
guard can otherwise be satisfied by adding a reason instead of a key, and
neither of those two has an acceptable reason to be absent.

**ALSO RECORDED: the e2e Verdict step fired in production for the sixth time.**

## 🔴 SECURITY 2026-10-13 (fifty-sixth entry) — slice 1 turned a log line into a free-pass minter, and the 2026-08-07 comment had already named the condition

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). **This is a hole I opened today, found by reading
the code I had changed the blast radius of.**

**THE PREVIOUS AUTHOR WROTE DOWN WHEN IT WOULD BECOME DANGEROUS.** From the
2026-08-07 fix comment at the webhook, left in place and unchanged since:

> "Today the handler only logs, so the blast radius is a false payment record in
> the logs — but the docstring names this the hook point for Supabase writes
> when feeSchedule moves server-side, **and at that point the same request marks
> a fee paid.**"

**That point arrived at 08:00 this morning, in slice 1.** `_grant_pass` writes
`public.event_passes`. The webhook's unverified branch — correct and deliberate
for a local dev box — accepts an unsigned body when `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is
unset. Every fact the grant needs comes **out of that body**: `event_id`,
`studio_id`, `payment_status`. So on a deployment with `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` set
and no signing secret, an unauthenticated POST to `/api/stripe/webhook` would
**mint a One-Event Pass for any event in any studio**. Yesterday the identical
request produced a log line.

**AND NOTHING COULD SAY WHETHER THAT WAS THE CASE.**
`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is read from the environment and is **not declared in
`render.yaml`** — so no file in this repo could answer it. "It is probably
configured in production" was the only thing standing between that route and
free passes, and that is not a control. The same blind spot
`/api/food-prices/status` exists for.

**THE FIX IS GATED ON VERIFICATION, NOT ON ENVIRONMENT.** An entitlement is
never granted from an unverified body — full stop, no environment sniffing, no
`if RENDER`. The unverified path still exists for a genuine dev box, still
announces itself, still logs the event; it simply cannot hand out an
entitlement, and it logs `REFUSING … Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` at ERROR. A dev
who needs to exercise the grant runs `stripe listen`, which issues a real
`whsec_` and is the documented way anyway. Still returns 2xx, so Stripe is not
given a reason to retry forever.

**THE EXISTING TESTS WERE PASSING AGAINST A PATH PRODUCTION NEVER TAKES.**
`test_stripe_pass_entitlement.py`'s `dev_webhook` fixture set
`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET = ""` on purpose, "so these tests exercise the GRANT, not
signature verification". Reasonable when written on 2026-10-13 morning; wrong by
the afternoon. All fourteen grant assertions were driving the unverified branch.
The fixture now verifies for real (`construct_event` monkeypatched to parse the
body), which is the path a live purchase travels. **Two new tests, and the
second is what makes the first mean anything:** an unverified webhook writes
nothing, and *the identical body* grants once the signature verifies.

**TWO INSTRUMENTS, BECAUSE "UNATTESTED" WAS THE REAL PROBLEM.**
· `GET /api/stripe/status` now returns `webhook_verified` and
  `can_honour_purchases` — booleans only, never values. One curl replaces a
  dashboard login, and a test asserts no secret material appears in the payload.
· `/api/capabilities` now reports `stripe_can_honour_purchases`, and the pass
  sheet's `canCharge` requires it. **This is the audit's core finding made
  enforceable** — "flipping `REACT_APP_BILLING_LIVE` would take money and
  deliver nothing recoverable" is a thing no client-side flag can know.

**THE THREE-STATE FLAG IS NOT FUSSINESS.** It is `true | false | null`, and the
test reads `!== false`. `null` means the one-shot capabilities fetch has not
answered. A two-state version reads false on first paint, so the sheet would
show "free while in preview" and swap to a **$39 button** a moment later — two
different claims about price on the one surface where that is unacceptable. An
unknown changes nothing; only a confirmed false suppresses. `commApi` likewise
records it only when the backend actually sent a boolean, so a deployment that
has not shipped the new key stays `null` instead of hiding the button
everywhere.

**MEASUREMENT NOTE, STATED BECAUSE IT QUALIFIES THE BACKEND NUMBER.** pytest
cannot be installed here as pinned: `asyncpg==0.29.0` has no wheel for this
container's Python 3.13 and fails to build. The suite was run against
**asyncpg 0.32.0**, installed locally only — `requirements.txt` is untouched.
For these tests asyncpg is imported and never used (the pool is a fake), so the
version is immaterial to the result, but the run was not against the pinned
tree and that is worth knowing before trusting the number.

**QA.** backend pytest **440 passed** — and note the row below said **399**
since 2026-10-02, so that figure was stale by 41 before today. jest
**606 suites / 8,336 passed**, 1 skipped (+4). `gate:cra` green, 241 of 241.
hostv2 build green with the parity gate. vitest **49 / 4**.
`check:migrations` green.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, AND IT IS NOW THE TOP OPERATIONAL ITEM:** whether
`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is actually set on Render, and whether the Stripe
endpoint subscribes `checkout.session.completed`. Both are now *checkable* —
`curl .../api/stripe/status` answers the first — but neither is *checked*. Until
they are, the honest statement is that this deployment cannot honour a purchase,
and the shell will now say so by refusing to show the button.

## FIXED 2026-10-13 (fifty-fifth entry) — the sheet that sold what you owned, and an index covering a quarter of its subject

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). Follow-on from slice 3, in the same session.

**THE SHEET OFFERED TO SELL A PASS THE EVENT ALREADY HELD.** `canCharge` answers
"may this deployment take money", which is not the question "does this host owe
any" — and nothing asked the second one. An owner opened the pass sheet to a
**"Get the pass — $39"** button. Slice 3's new 409 toast caught it after the tap,
which made the refusal honest and left the button a lie (UX_07: a CTA may not
offer a charge that cannot legitimately be taken). `passHeld(event)` is now
checked FIRST, ahead of both other states — ahead of `canCharge` so it is never
sold twice, and ahead of the preview state, because telling someone who paid
that the app is "free while in preview" is the same untruth pointed the other
way. The owned copy deliberately does **not** say "confirmed with Stripe": when
only the event's own record claims the pass, that sentence would invent a
confirmation. A test asserts the absence of that phrasing.

**THE AUDIT THAT DROVE ALL THREE SLICES WAS NEVER RE-OPENED.**
`docs/audits/2026-10-03_STRIPE_CONSUMER_CHECKOUT_READINESS.md` named five gaps
and recommended treating consumer checkout as **unbuilt**. All five are now
closed in code, and the document still said otherwise — which is how an audit
becomes the thing that sends the next person to rebuild what exists. It now
carries a re-measurement block at the top, each gap with a verdict and what
closed it, and the original text untouched below.

**AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE AUDIT'S OWN RANKING.** It filed the
caller-supplied price third of five, "small beside" the entitlement store. That
was wrong: it was not a latent property of a router nobody called, it was
**shipped code in the product's own pass sheet**. It was the one gap already
written.

**WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, AND NONE OF IT IS CODE** — recorded in the audit so the
next reader meets it there, not here:
· the live `public.event_passes` table is **UNATTESTED** (the merge landed and

· the **Stripe webhook endpoint subscription is UNATTESTED, and is now the

## FIXED 2026-10-13 (fifty-fourth entry) — the price was coming from the browser, in shipped code

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). Slice 3 of three. **This is the only slice of the
three that fixes a live defect rather than building toward one.**

**WHAT I FOUND WHEN I OPENED THE PASS SHEET.** Slice 3 was scoped as "wire the
pass sheet to `create-pass-session`", on the assumption the sheet had no
checkout. It had one, and it was this:

```js
createCheckoutSession({ amountCents: 3900,
                        feeId: 'one-event-pass-' + event.id, … })
```

That is **gap #3 of `docs/audits/2026-10-03_STRIPE_CONSUMER_CHECKOUT_READINESS.md`
living in the shell** — "the price cannot come from the caller" — and it was not
hypothetical: a buyer who edited the bundle posted one cent and received the
same entitlement. `amount_cents` is CORRECT for a planner's own fee, where the
planner sets the number, and `App.js` still uses it that way. On a fixed-price
product the same property is the hole.

`createPassSession({ eventId })` replaces it. **No amount, no label, no
fee id** — the server charges `PASS_AMOUNT_CENTS`, and
`PassSessionRequest.model_fields` is asserted to be exactly
`{event_id, success_url, cancel_url}`. hostv2 no longer **imports**
`createCheckoutSession` at all: an import is an invitation, and this shell sells
one thing at one price.

**THE RETURN TRIP NO LONGER VERIFIES A PAYMENT, BECAUSE IT NO LONGER HAS TO.**
The old handler called `verifySession` and matched a metadata `fee_id`. A pass
session's metadata carries `kind: 'pass'` and no `fee_id`, so that check could
only ever fail. More to the point, the entitlement row is written **only** by
the signature-verified webhook — so the row IS the proof and the redirect is
evidence of nothing. The pass branch now calls
`refreshEventPass(eventId, { claimed: true })` and reads `serverPassHeld`.
`claimed` because the host has just come back from a completed checkout, which
is precisely the webhook/redirect race slice 2 built the provisional-no for.

**THE LEGACY RETURN SHAPE IS NOT DELETED, AND THAT IS NOT TIDINESS.** A Stripe
receipt email is permanent, and the handler's own copy tells people to reopen
the app from it. `?stripe_paid=1&fee_id=one-event-pass-…` stays parsed and still
verify-first; `?pass_paid=1&event_id=…` is the new shape. Deleting the old
branch would turn a real receipt into a link that silently does nothing.

**THE BLOB IS NOW ONLY EVER A CACHE OF A CONFIRMED FACT.** Both success paths
write `passPurchased: true` through one `unlocked()` helper and neither failure
path does — so the shell cannot manufacture the claim that `passGate` falls back
to. A test counts the occurrences and asserts the single write is inside that
helper.

**TWO GUARDS CAUGHT ME, AND BOTH WERE RIGHT.**

1. **`plannerFetchesCarryAuth` had a hole I put there.** `/api/stripe/pass`
   shipped a caller in slice 1 and I never added it to that file's `GATED` list.
   Both pass routes call `require_planner`, and `fetchEventPass`'s whole job is
   to answer "does this event hold a pass" — unauthenticated that is a 401 or,
   far worse, an answer for the wrong tenant. Added, one route and several hours
   later than it should have been.
2. **`textGateRatchet` refused the new test file** (54 gates, baseline 53) and
   demanded a justification rather than a bump. It deserves one: the claim is an
   **absence** — that no amount is posted and that `createCheckoutSession` is
   not imported — and a rendered assertion cannot observe a field that is not
   sent. The surface is also unreachable: billing is dormant, so the sheet
   renders its "free while in preview" state and there is no checkout button for
   an e2e to press. A test that waits for D-2 to flip a flag before it can fail
   is not a guard. Raised to 54 with that written above the constant, in the
   file's own idiom.

**ALSO WORTH KNOWING:** the new suite's first run failed on its own
documentation — the matcher for `amountCents:` hit the comment that QUOTES the
old call. Comments are now stripped before the source-shape match. And
`stripeApi` captures `BASE` at **import** time (the wart `isBillingLive()`
exists to dodge), so the module is loaded after the env is set rather than at
the top of the file; the first draft threw "No API backend configured" on every

## BUILT 2026-10-13 (fifty-third entry) — the shell asks, and the race that arrives with the money

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). Slice 2 of three, authorized by name ("slice 2").
Slice 1 is the entry below; read it first — it is where the precedence rules
and the rejected rule are.

**TWO EDITS IN THE SHELL, AND BOTH GUARDS ARE LOAD-BEARING.**
`HostShellV2.jsx` now asks the server once per event open:

```js
usePassEntitlement(eventId);                       // the re-render seam
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isBillingLive()) return;
  if (!eventId || !isUserCreatedEvent({ id: eventId })) return;
  refreshEventPass(eventId, { claimed: passClaimed });
}, [eventId, passClaimed]);
```

`isBillingLive()` — dormant in production, so this fires for nobody today;
asking anyway would be a request per event open for an answer no gate consults.
`isUserCreatedEvent` — the route resolves the tenant key from a `public.events`
row, which only the host's own events have, so a sample would collect a 409 that
means nothing. That is the engine's own predicate, not a second definition of
the same idea.

**THE RE-RENDER SEAM WAS A REAL GAP, FOUND BY LOOKING AT EVERY CALL SITE RATHER
THAN ASSUMING.** `passGate` is synchronous and reads the module store directly —
which is what lets `briefAllowed` work inside a tap handler with no prop
plumbing. But nothing told React when an answer landed:

| Gate | Where it is called | Needs a re-render |
|---|---|---|
| `briefAllowed` | `:3665`, inside the async share-brief handler | **no** — reads at tap time |
| `destinationLocked` | `:14580`, `:15946`, `:16129`, all inside sheet-render IIFEs | **yes** |

So a teased lodging/ground/arrivals surface would have stayed teased after the
server confirmed the pass, until something unrelated re-rendered it. React here
is **19.2.6**, so the fix is `subscribePassEntitlements` + `useSyncExternalStore`
— not an epoch counter, and not moving the store into component state. The
subscriber fires only when an answer actually *changes*, so a repeat "yes" costs
no render.

**THE RACE THAT ARRIVES WITH THE MONEY, AND WHY IT IS HANDLED HERE RATHER THAN
DEFERRED.** Stripe redirects the browser and POSTs the webhook **independently**.
If the redirect wins, the host lands with a blob that claims a pass and an
`event_passes` table that has no row yet — and the refresh this slice adds would
read `held: false` and **revoke the unlock of someone who paid seconds ago**.
Adding the refresh without handling this would have shipped that defect, and it
is reachable the moment D-2 flips the billing flag.

`refreshEventPass(id, { claimed })` makes a "no" **provisional** while the blob
claims a pass: it re-asks on a bounded backoff (`CLAIM_RETRY_DELAYS_MS =
[2000, 4000]` — two delays, **three asks total, a confirmation and not a poll**)
before writing it down. A "yes" is never retried. A **failure** is never
retried into a revocation either. The cost of being wrong the other way is two
extra requests: a stale or hand-edited claim re-asks twice, gets the same "no",
and is revoked — the right side to be wrong on when the subject is a $39 charge.

**AN IN-FLIGHT ASK HAD TO BECOME UPGRADEABLE.** On a paid return the shell asks
on mount, *before* the return handler has written the claim, and again a beat
later with `claimed: true`. Handing the second caller the first caller's promise
applies the FIRST call's policy, so the race's "no" gets written down as a
revocation anyway — the dedupe defeating the fix. The flag now lives in a record
the running loop re-reads. Two tests pin it, and the second is the negative:
**identical mock, identical ordering, no second caller → the "no" IS written**.
A guard whose absence changes nothing is not a guard.

**The retry cadence is an option on the function, not a constant closed over**,
so the tests run the real retry path in milliseconds instead of hand-flushing
microtasks through three awaited fetches and two awaited timers. CRA's jest has
no `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` — the first draft used it and failed. A test pins
`CLAIM_RETRY_DELAYS_MS` to `[2000, 4000]` so the production cadence is still
asserted and cannot quietly widen into a poll.

**NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGES.** `isBillingLive()` is false
(`REACT_APP_BILLING_LIVE` unset), so the effect never fires. The hook runs
always and reads an empty Map.

**QA.** jest **604 suites / 8,312 passed**, 1 skipped (+12 over slice 1).
`gate:cra` green — **241 of 241 baselined, no new warnings**. hostv2
`npm run build` green including the className-parity gate (3 kit atoms, 11 hero

**NOT TOUCHED, DELIBERATELY:** the paid-return handler at `:3450`. It verifies a

`kind: 'pass'` metadata. Pointing it at the pass flow is slice 3, together with

## BUILT 2026-10-13 (fifty-second entry) — passGate reads the server record, and the rule I floated for it was wrong

Times Eastern (EDT, UTC−4). Slice 1 of three, authorized by the owner by name
("next slice: passGate reads the server record").

**WHAT WAS ALREADY TRUE, AND WHY THE SLICE IS SMALLER THAN THE AUDIT IMPLIED.**
`passGate` did not lack the concept of a purchased pass — `briefAllowed` and
`destinationLocked` have both read `ev.passPurchased` since the engine landed,
and the hostv2 return handler that writes it (`HostShellV2.jsx:3412-3430`) is
already stricter than "trust the redirect": it requires a session id, calls
`verifySession`, and demands `payment_status === 'paid'` AND a matching metadata
`fee_id`. What it cannot survive is a closed tab or a cleared browser, because
the answer lived only in that browser's copy of the event.

| Change | File |
|---|---|
| `fetchEventPass(eventId)` → `GET /api/stripe/pass` | `src/lib/stripeApi.js` — same auth/error idiom as `verifySession` |
| The server's answers, held in memory, with `refreshEventPass` / `serverPassHeld` / `recordServerPass` | `src/lib/passEntitlement.js` (new) |
| `passHeld(ev)` → `{ held, source }`; both gates now go through it | `src/lib/passGate.js` |
| `/api/stripe/pass` removed from `BUILT_NOT_WIRED` — it has a caller now | `everyBackendRouteHasACaller.test.js` |
| 15 new tests | `src/lib/__tests__/passEntitlement.test.js` (new) |

**I FLOATED A RULE AND THEN REJECTED IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING.** What
I told the owner before building was: "server truth when available; last
server-confirmed value in memory otherwise; **never grant from the persisted
event blob**." The last clause is wrong and I did not ship it. Refusing to grant
while the server has not yet answered buys **no security** — `passGate` runs in
the browser, and anyone willing to edit the bundle returns `allowed: true` from
any of it — while it costs a host who has genuinely paid their unlock on every
cold load and every offline minute. The real boundary is the route, not the
gate: an `event_passes` row can only be created by the signature-verified Stripe
webhook. So the shipped precedence is:

- server answered **true** → held, `source: 'server'`
- server answered **false** → **NOT held, whatever the blob says** (revocation)
- server **never answered** → the blob's claim stands, `source: 'claim'`

What the server record actually buys is **recovery** (a paid host keeps their
unlock across a cleared browser or a second device) and **revocation** (a stale
or hand-edited `passPurchased` stops granting). Those are the two things the
blob could never do. Both directions are pinned by tests; the rejected rule is
written into `passEntitlement.js` as a paragraph explaining why not to re-adopt
it, because the headline version is more persuasive than the correct version.

**A FAILED LOOKUP RECORDS NOTHING.** A 403, a cold backend or a dropped
connection must not be written down as `held: false` — that would revoke a real
purchase on a network blip, the worst outcome this module can produce. Only a
successful response with a boolean `held` is recorded. Two tests pin it.

**THE RULING'S CLAUSES ARE UNCHANGED.** All 13 existing `passGate` tests pass
untouched, including both that assert `passPurchased: true` unlocks — the pass
still unlocks the whole event, only the SOURCE of the fact changed. NEVER
MID-CONVERSATION still outranks a server "no": a brief already shared is an open
conversation with a real vendor, and a test now pins that too. Billing-dormant
still short-circuits everything ahead of any of this.

**NO RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR CHANGES YET, DELIBERATELY.** Nothing calls
`refreshEventPass`, so `serverPassHeld` returns `null` for every event and both
gates behave exactly as they did this morning. The new `'pass-claimed'` reason
only ever appears on an ALLOWED answer, and the one consumer
(`HostShellV2.jsx:3641`) branches on `!gate.allowed` and `'second-vendor'` only
— checked, not assumed. Slice 2 (hostv2 calls `refreshEventPass` on event open)
is what makes any of this visible.

`gate:cra` green — **241 of 241 baselined, no new warnings** (a bare
`CI=true react-scripts build` "fails" on those 241 pre-existing warnings; the

this slice.

**STILL UNWIRED, BY DECISION:** `/api/stripe/create-pass-session`. The pass
sheet is what should call it, and that is slice 3.

## BUILT 2026-10-13 (fiftieth entry) — the server-side entitlement, so a purchase can survive a cleared browser

PR #87 merged (`3ae5c6d`). Branch restarted from the new `main` per the
merged-PR rule. Owner picked the sequence and the scope: merge first, then
**backend spine only** — no `passGate` change, no hostv2, billing still dormant.

**What was wrong.** `2026-10-03_STRIPE_CONSUMER_CHECKOUT_READINESS.md` answered
D-2 #3 with *no*: Stripe is "live, hardened and working — for a different job"
(billing a host's CLIENT for a fee) and cannot sell the One-Event Pass. The
blocker, in the 2026-08-07 ruling's own words already sitting in the router:
*"There is no server-side entitlement (feeSchedule is localStorage and the
webhook only logs), so an anonymous purchase produces a charge and nothing the
host can ever recover."* Clearing the browser lost the purchase; editing
localStorage granted it free. **Ten days, nothing built, no design posted.**

**Built.** `supabase/migrations/017_event_passes.sql` — the CANONICAL folder,
not `backend/migrations`, which its own README freezes as legacy; a shared
table there would have tripped `check:migrations`. One row per event
(`event_id` primary key) because the ruling says *"whichever door fired, one
pass unlocks that whole event"*. `studio_id` is the tenant key; `purchased_by`
is audit attribution and never an access decision. RLS on with **no policy**,
so no client reaches it — the only writer is a signature-verified webhook,
which is the whole of "editing localStorage grants it for free", closed.

**Three design calls worth keeping:**

| Call | Why |
|---|---|
| A SEPARATE route (`create-pass-session`), not a mode flag | `create-checkout-session` takes `amount_cents` from the caller, which is CORRECT for a planner invoicing their own client, and the audit's gap #3 for a fixed-price product. Two products, so two routes — a flag would leave a fixed price one boolean from a caller-set one. The pass request has **no price field at all**; the test asserts the field set exactly |
| NO foreign keys on the table | Every delete rule is wrong for a receipt: `cascade` destroys the evidence somebody paid when an event or studio is deleted; restricting breaks unrelated deletes. Integrity comes from the write path, same argument `013_vendor_brief_links.sql` makes |
| The webhook GRANTS; the redirect only informs | `success_url` carries the session id and the UI calls `/verify-session` — good signal, bad grant: the user controls whether their browser returns, so a closed tab would mean a charge with no pass. And this branch does **not** swallow errors the way the fee branch does; a 2xx on a failed write means Stripe never retries and a paying customer has nothing |

**14 new tests, `test_stripe_pass_entitlement.py`, red-proofed both ways.** The
one that matters most: **the money route never claims event ownership.**
`communication._assert_event_access` claims an unowned event for the caller's
studio on first touch — correct for comms, catastrophic on a route that then
charges a card. That is PR #86's hole with a receipt attached, so
`_studio_for_event` is deliberately STRICTER than the shared helper rather than
a reuse of it: the event must have a `public.events` row, and an unsynced event
is refused with its own status and a message saying so, because "you don't have
access" would be a lie — the host does own it, the server has never seen it.

Verified: backend **437 passed** (was 423, +14). Route sweep green, so both new
routes gate their caller and answer 401 bare. `check:migrations` green. Red-proof
driven in both directions — dropping the `payment_status == "paid"` check fails
the unpaid test, adding `amount_cents` back fails the price-shape test.

⚠️ **MERGING THIS APPLIES THE MIGRATION.** `supabase/migrations` is the folder
the Supabase GitHub integration WATCHES — merge to `main` applies `017` to the
live project. It is additive (one new table, no changes to existing schema) and
nothing reads it yet, but it is a live schema change, not a file.

**Still NOT sellable, and this entry does not claim otherwise.** The spine
stores an entitlement; nothing consumes it. `passGate` still answers "allowed"
while billing is dormant and has not been pointed at this table. hostv2 still
has no Stripe code. Remaining before money: `passGate` reads the server record,
hostv2 wiring, the pass sheet → checkout, then D-2 #1/#2/#4/#5 — all four
owner-side.
